mcp.plain: The Model Context Protocol, a standard way for an AI assistant to call tools that another program offers.
mcp.analogy: the standard plug that lets any assistant use the shop.

sandbox.plain: A closed-off container where a tool runs, with limits on what it can reach.

manifest.plain: The file in a tool package that names its inputs, network hosts and secrets.
manifest.analogy: the label stating what the tool may touch.

schema_fuzzing.plain: Trying many unusual inputs that the tool says it accepts, to find crashes and hangs.
schema_fuzzing.analogy: the inspector pulling every lever in odd ways to see what breaks.

egress.plain: Network traffic that leaves the room where a tool runs.
egress.analogy: anything that goes out through the door of the test room.

decoy_credentials.plain: Fake passwords and keys, planted so that any attempt to take them shows.
decoy_credentials.analogy: fake keys left lying around to see who reaches for them.

ledger.plain: A record of events that is only added to, never rewritten.
ledger.analogy: the notebook where every inspection and every call is written down.

hash_chain.plain: Each entry carries a fingerprint of the one before, so changing an old entry breaks the check.
hash_chain.analogy: numbered pages stitched together, where a swapped page shows.

quarantine.plain: A state that stops a tool version from running until a person releases it.
quarantine.analogy: taking a tool off the shelf and locking it in the back room.

operator.plain: The person who runs ToolForge and is the only one who can promote, approve or release a tool.
operator.analogy: the person who holds the keys and signs off.

blast_radius.plain: A report of what a tool was seen doing and what it could have reached, with unmeasured parts marked.
blast_radius.analogy: the inspector's report on the damage a tool could do.
